clue.text: People turning up with nothing in position

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces before it go inside the word for position

parts.note: a place is a position
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: turning means the little word up is flipped round to read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone climbs from nothing into a position of standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' is the reversal signal for 'up', and 'in' the container signal; 'People' is the definition, not part of the picture of someone rising.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the ordinary mass of inhabitants, the common people.

clue.text: Rock climbing. I am dressed in purple

indicators.note: dressed in says the piece before goes inside the colour word

parts.note: puce is a purplish brown colour

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, means the letters are written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am

explanation.surface: A climber on a rock says they are wearing purple.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means read upwards; 'Rock climbing' looks like a sport, but only 'Rock' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light, porous volcanic stone.

clue.text: Criticize attempt to provide store cupboard

parts.note: to pan is to criticize harshly
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone attacks an effort to build a larder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard where food is kept.

clue.text: It's not quite the thing, interrupting without levity

indicators.note: interrupting says the scrambled piece breaks into the word for without

parts.note: less means without, as in 'less sugar'

indicators.note: not quite suggests the letters of thing are not quite in order, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Something improper intrudes, and humour is lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' is an unusual anagram signal: the thing is not quite right, so jumbled; 'interrupting' is the container signal and 'It's' and 'the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is frivolity, a want of seriousness or weight.

clue.text: Fell policeman holding broken camera

indicators.note: holding says the word for policeman wraps round the rearranged letters

parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: broken says the letters of camera are rearranged

explanation.surface: A constable grips a smashed camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' signals the anagram and 'holding' the container; 'Fell' is a verb, past tense, matching the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is an idiom for falling heavily, or failing badly.

clue.text: A fellow is a dandy

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that some man is a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adonis is a strikingly handsome young man, the sort of beau a dandy aims to be.

clue.text: Up in Cumbria, a road is made longer

indicators.note: Up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Cumbria is a county in the north-west of England, NW

explanation.surface: A Cumbrian road has been extended.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in north-west England, hence NW; 'Up' turns NWARD into DRAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn out means stretched or prolonged.

clue.text: Don and Jack don't finish the race

parts.note: nob is the card-playing name for the jack of trumps in cribbage

indicators.note: don't finish says the final letter of the race's name is dropped

parts.note: Le Mans is the famous motor race, le being French for the

explanation.surface: Two racers fail to complete the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' is the Spanish title of a gentleman; LE MANS, the 24-hour race, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman of rank, a peer.

clue.text: The saintliness of the untouchable?

parts.note: read as the quality of something sacrosanct, too holy to be touched

explanation.surface: A question about the virtue of a social outcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untouchable' suggests an Indian caste, but here means inviolable, beyond touching.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is holiness and inviolability, being sacred.

clue.text: Single union attains this record high

parts.note: a mono record is one recorded on a single channel
game meat that is high, slightly off, is gamy

explanation.surface: A wedding that breaks a record for altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Monogamy is marriage to only one partner at a time, a single union.

clue.text: Copy industrial diamond without difficulty

indicators.note: without tells us one word is removed from the longer word for the diamond

parts.note: carbonado is a black diamond used in industry for drilling
ado is fuss or difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone easily reproduces a gemstone used in industry.
explanation.walkthrough: CARBONADO, a dark industrial diamond, loses ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon is a copy made with carbon paper, a duplicate.

clue.text: Permit a race, in small part, to occasion gossip

indicators.note: in says the pieces before it sit inside the word for small part

parts.note: a tittle is a tiny amount, a jot
to let is to permit
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Allowing a race, even partly, sets tongues wagging.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race; 'in' puts the run permit-a-race inside the word for a small part.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle is idle chatter, rumour.

clue.text: Painter takes care of rubbish

parts.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: An artist looks after the garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: Camille COROT was a French landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Corot was a nineteenth-century French landscape artist.

clue.text: Lamenting changes in taking sides

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grieving over shifts in partisan loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Alignment is siding with a party or group, picking an allegiance.

clue.text: Intimate the necessity of following suit

explanation.surface: A heart-to-heart chat about having to copy others.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games you must follow suit, so a heart led requires a heart to be played on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A frank personal talk is intimate; in cards a heart led calls for a heart in reply, playing to suit.

clue.text: Most Irish characters are so casual

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the preceding words, taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Irish people are mostly relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard, careless or random is casual.

clue.text: Food in a restaurant is usually obtainable without effort

definitions.text: Food in a restaurant is usually

explanation.surface: Restaurant meals are easy to come by.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant dishes are served on crockery; an idiom for something handed over with no work.

clue.text: Not immoderate, deranged or insane

indicators.note: deranged suggests disorder, so the letters of the words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Neither extreme, unhinged nor mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Within reason means within sensible limits, moderate.

clue.text: The most beautiful flower?

parts.note: read as a plant name meaning that no other is so lovely: the old cottage-garden name for London pride

explanation.surface: A question about which bloom is loveliest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a cryptic definition: a flower whose name boasts that nothing rivals it.
explanation.definitionFit: London pride, a saxifrage, is popularly called by a name claiming nothing matches its beauty.

clue.text: Discourage mother bird

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A mother bird puts off its young.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen spirits is to discourage or dishearten.

clue.text: Sung a number of times

parts.note: read as describing music performed by many voices together

explanation.surface: Something repeated over and over in song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number' suggests repetition, but means many people singing at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is sung by a choir, a group of voices.

clue.text: Flower power backed some remarkable events

indicators.note: backed says the two pieces together are read from the end to the start

parts.note: the anemone is a flower
hp is horsepower, a unit of power

explanation.surface: Flower power enjoyed some remarkable moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns both pieces together; 'Flower power' poses as the hippy slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are striking or extraordinary occurrences.

clue.text: Every other one of the Roman ships found refuge

indicators.note: every other one says to take alternate letters, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Alternate Roman vessels reached a safe haven.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of ROMANSHIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, a place of shelter.

clue.text: Fish left out of 20's order

indicators.note: order says the letters are rearranged once one is removed

parts.note: 20 down's answer is a word meaning sung

explanation.surface: A fish is dropped from a sung arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CHORAL (20 down), remove L, and 'order' rearranges CHORA as ROACH.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Help from Cordelia's sister

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: Aid from a sibling of King Lear's youngest daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Cordelia's sisters are Goneril and Regan, but the answer sits in the letters across 'Cordelia's sister'.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help or give aid.

clue.text: An entertainer, in a way an admirable person

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a ripper is old slang for a splendid person or thing

explanation.surface: A performer is a fine person in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPPER is dated British and Australian slang for something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper performs a striptease, a kind of entertainment.

clue.text: The chap to resent change

indicators.note: change says the letters of the word before it are shuffled

explanation.surface: A man who is inclined to resent any alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so a chap.

clue.text: A child comes in close at certain times

indicators.note: comes in says the pieces before it go inside the word for close

parts.note: to seal is to close
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A little one arrives at the end at particular moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is the verb (to SEAL), not 'near' or 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal means occurring at particular times of the year.
